'''Mandalorian''' was the [[Writing/Legends|written form]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]], the spoken [[Language/Legends|language]] of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]]. It was also used to read and write [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]].

==Description==
The Mandalorian [[Writing/Legends|writing system]] consisted of twenty-six characters and was used to provide a written analog to the spoken [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]]. Despite there being no F, X, or Z equivalents in the verbal Mando'a, these letters were included in the written alphabet for greater ease in transliterating foreign words.<ref name="The Mandalorians: People and Culture">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> Mandalorian also allowed for use of a base 10 number system with numerals denoted 0 through 9.<ref name="SWArchive">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/feature/20020716/indexp2.html|text=''Holographic'' Artist: Philip Metschan|date=2002-07-16}} <small>([[:File:MandalorianWritingSystem-SWcom.png|image of the Mandalorian alphabet]], not captured by the [[Wikipedia:Wayback Machine|Wayback Machine]])</small></ref>

Traditional Mandalorian groups, such as the [[True Mandalorians]], used [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]] to record and display written information on personal [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]] and [[Starship/Legends|ship]]-board display screens. They also painted sigils on their [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|helmets]] to signify status or condition. The Mando'a characters for M and S were often painted to identify Mandalorians suffering ''mir'shupur'' (brain damage). This served to inform other Mandos of their condition and also as a form of battle commendation.<ref name="Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

Use of Mando'a in this form was continued by traditional Mandalorian groups such as the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]].<ref name="The Mandalorians: People and Culture" />

Mandalorian also appeared to be the standard writing system used by the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]].<ref name="Corruption" /> However, they relied little on ''Mando'a'', if at all, to communicate amongst themselves and as such, instances of written Mandalorian by the New Mandalorians could often be translated directly into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]].<ref name="The Academy" /> The [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] were also known to employ Mandalorian in the writing of Basic.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />

==History==
[[File:Slave_I_display.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Console displaying ''Mandalorian'' as used by Jango Fett]]Prior to the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Mandalorian [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] relied heavily upon written Mandalorian to display relevant information on the ship-board displays of his [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft/Legends|''Firespray'' gunship]] ''[[Slave I/Legends|SLave I]]''.<ref name="AOTC" />

----
<center>''During the Clone Wars, an alternative Mandalorian typeface was widely used. The letters 'M' and 'V' exhibited entirely distinct designs, while the character 'P' possessed a somewhat altered shape, and the letters 'C' and 'X' differed slightly.<ref name="The Academy" /><ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /><ref name="Corruption" /><ref name="Evil Plans" /> Some numbers differed as well, with the digits 0,<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /><ref name="Corruption" /> 1<ref name="The Academy"/><ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /><ref name="Corruption" /> and 2 having a completely different design,<ref name="Corruption" /> and the number 7 looking like the standard digit 1.''<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /><ref name="Corruption" /></center></center>
----

As [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizla]] was communicating with [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] in the [[Death Watch hideout]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]], Mandalorian writing appeared on two [[holochart]]s. One monitor included the text "[[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|TARGET]]: [[Peace Park/Legends|PEACE PARK]]." The other monitor said:<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />


<center><poem>[[Coronet/Legends|''CORONET'']]
[[Duchess/Legends|DUTTHESS]] <small>''[sic]''</small> [[Satine Kryze/Legends|SATINE]]

ARRIVES
[[Sundari/Legends|SUNDARI]] [[Spaceport/Legends|SPACEPORT]]

DOCK NUMBER 01
PROCESS AS PLAN <small>''[sic]''</small></poem></center>


[[File:SlabinMolecule-Corruption.png|thumb|right|150px|A computer representation of the slabin molecular structure used by the New Mandalorians]]Fittingly, the writing on the second holochart was accompanied by a picture of Satine's [[Transport/Legends|luxury spaceliner]].<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />

[[Buirk'alor-class airspeeder|Mandalorian police speeders]] displayed the phrase "TO PROTECT AND SERVE" on their windshields, with the word "[[Law enforcement agency|POLICE]]" prominently featured at the front.<ref name="Corruption" /> 

A [[Unidentified Mandalorian customs official/Legends|corrupt customs official]] wore a crest on their [[Limb/Legends|shoulder]] that read "[[New Mandalorian customs department|MANDALORE CUSTOMS]]."<ref name="Corruption">{{TCW|Corruption (episode)}}</ref>

The [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|New Mandalorian hospital]] used Mandalorian in their research. One of the [[Computer/Legends|computer]] monitors in their research laboratory erroneously used the letter 'S' instead of 'L,' resulting in several misspellings. It read: <ref name="Corruption" />

A computer in [[Siddiq/Legends|Siddiq's]] office at the [[Unidentified Mandalorian shipping company/Legends|shipping company]] said "ROUTES SCHEDULE." When Siddiq logged into the computer, they typed in the word "ARRIVAL." Following Siddiq's login, the monitor once more showed the words "ROUTES SCHEDULE" in addition to various other information. The computer also featured a Mandalorian keyboard that displayed all numbers from 0 to 9, 26 letters, and several punctuation marks:<ref name="Corruption" />

The students at the [[Royal Academy of Government/Legends|Royal Academy of Government]] used standard [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]] that said "ALLIGNMENT" <small>''[sic]''</small> at the top and "READY" at the bottom. However, one student, [[Soniee/Legends|Soniee]], utilized a special datapad that employed [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] script rather than Mandalorian. Mandalorian also appeared on on the screens mounted on the walls of the dormitory that Soniee shared with her fellow [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]].<ref name="The Academy" />

An unidentified [[Prisoner/Legends|inmate]] at the [[Royal prison/Legends|royal prison]] on Mandalore wore a [[Clothing/Legends|prison uniform]] reading "[[THX 1137/Legends|THX 1137]]."<ref name="The Academy" />

The [[Mandalorian secret service/Legends|Mandalorian Secret Service]] displayed Aurebesh numerals on their [[Riot shield/Legends|riot shields]]<ref name="The Academy" /> while wearing a crest on their left shoulder that read "IN DEFENSE OF MANDALORE."<ref name="Academy Guide" /><ref name="Academy Archive">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode306.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Academy|date=2010-10-15}}</ref> 

Two shops in the [[Lower market districts/Legends|lower market districts]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] had luminous [[Color/Legends|yellow]] Mandalorian letters applied to a large, smoking chimney on top of the roof. The sign exhibited the name of the establishment, "[[Snack/Legends|SNACK]]."<ref name="Evil Plans" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Original font===
{{Quote|From the beginning of the trilogy George insisted that there be no English characters. I designed 3 new typefaces for EP2 one for the StarWars76 (Joe Johnston), Mandelorian <small>''[sic]''</small>, and one for the Geonosians.|Philip Metschan|<ref name="Portfolio" />}}

Prior to [[2002]], a typeface consisting of narrow vertical characters was developed to represent the written form of the Mandalorian language. It was developed by [[Philip Metschan]] at the request of [[George Lucas]] to be used in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']],<ref name="Portfolio">{{WebCite|url=http://www.principiagraphica.com/portfolio.htm|text=Philip Metschan's online portfolio|archivedate=20080718141854|nolive=1}}</ref><ref name="SWArchive" /> where the Mandalorian alphabet appears on the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] monitors of [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett's]] [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']].<ref name="AOTC" /> 

This typeface, erroneously named "Mandelorian" by Metschan, was created in conjunction with the further development of Joe Johnston's [[Unidentified script (Star Wars '76)|Star Wars '76]] (originally developed during the [[original trilogy]]) as well as a [[Geonosian (writing system)/Legends|Geonosian]] typeface that can be seen woven into the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star Plans]]. Metschan's typeface is often seen as using the same character for 'C' and 'U.' This is not the case and upon closer inspection it can be seen that there is a subtle difference between these two characters.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.metschanmedia.com/philip_metschan//portfolio.htm|text=Star Wars Typefaces|work=Philip Metschan's portfolio|nobackup=1}}</ref>

For the [[2004]] [[Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|Original Trilogy DVD]] release, artist [[Van Ling]]<ref name="Van Ling">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/release/video/f20010927/index.html|text=Van Ling: On the DVD Menu|date=2002-09-27}}</ref> incorporated the Mandalorian typeface into a number of transitional screens within the DVD's menu system.<ref name="DVD menu">[[Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|''Star Wars Trilogy'' DVD]] menu</ref><ref name="Eric Schroeder new">{{WebCite|url=http://www.erikstormtrooper.com/mandalorian.htm|text=Mandalorian Font|work=Erikstormtrooper's Imperial Gallery|archivedate=20260821153149}}</ref>

A common misconception is that the written form of [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]] was developed by [[Karen Traviss]] and [[Jesse Harlin]] for the ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'' multimedia project. While they did develop the Mando'a spoken language and its associated grammatical rules, they are not responsible for its original written visual depiction. Karen Traviss often credits a 23-letter alphabet to Jesse Harlin. However, at the time, it is highly likely that he was simply working from an incomplete version of Metschan's typeface licensed to them by [[Lucasfilm]].<ref name="Karen">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/html/alphabet.htm|text=Alphabet © Lucasfilm 2006|author=[[Karen Traviss]]|quote=This is the Mando'a alphabet. I didn't create it, and I can't change or add to it, so please don't ask me to. It's Lucasfilm's property; copyright law applies. I can't give you permission to use it, and I can't advise on copyright law because I'm not a lawyer, but if I were, I'd charge such outrageous fees that you wouldn't be able to afford me anyway. This is only for your own private and ''personal'' amusement. Which means no posting this online, either, and it doesn't matter if you're not doing it for profit.  Go check the copyright page again. Don't abuse it, and then you won't lose it. Okay? This isn't new, of course. Most of it has already been posted (and even tattooed) elsewhere ages ago by fans who've used the AOTC visual dictionary. You'll note that there are letters which aren't in the original 23-letter alphabet as conceived by Jesse Harlin, like F, X and Z, but ''Mando'ade'' have to be able to spell out those pesky ''aruetyc'' names somehow...the grammar guide explains all that.|work=KarenTraviss.com|archivedate=20081015083252|nolive=1}}</ref> 

===''The Clone Wars'' font===
[[File:ErikstormtrooperMandalorianFanfont.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Version 1 of Eric Schroeder's fanmade font, which made it into ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'']]Metschan's original font<ref name="SWArchive" /> was not used for for the animated TV series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''.<ref name="The Academy" /><ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /><ref name="Corruption" /><ref name="Evil Plans" /> Instead, a fan-made Mandalorian font designed by Erik Schroeder<ref name="Eric Schroeder old">{{WebCite|url=http://www.erikstormtrooper.com/mandalorian.htm|text=Mandalorian Font|author=Erik Schroeder|work=Erikstormtrooper's Imperial Gallery|archivedate=20060506233635|nolive=1}}</ref> was utilized for the episodes "[[The Mandalore Plot]],"<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]],"<ref name="Corruption" /> "[[The Academy]],"<ref name="The Academy" /> and "[[Evil Plans]]."<ref name="Evil Plans" /> 

Schroeder's font contains a few noticeable differences<ref name="Eric Schroeder old" /> which were adopted by the TV series: The letters 'M' and 'V' exhibit entirely different designs, while the character 'P' possesses a somewhat altered shape, and the letters 'C' and 'X' differ slightly.<ref name="The Academy" /><ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /><ref name="Corruption" /><ref name="Evil Plans" /> All twenty-six letters of Schroeder's alphabet<ref name="Eric Schroeder old" /> appear on [[Siddiq/Legends|Siddiq's]] [[Computer/Legends|computer]] keyboard in "Corruption."<ref name="Corruption" />

Some of Schroeder's punctuation<ref name="Eric Schroeder old" /> was used as well, with a colon (:) and a full stop (.) appearing on a monitor in the [[Death Watch hideout]] in "The Mandalore Plot,"<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> while a slash (/) can be glimpsed on a computer screen in the [[Sundari Mandalorian hospital/Legends|Sundari Mandalorian hospital]] in "The Academy."<ref name="The Academy" /> Siddiq's computer keyboard in "Corruption" features punctuation marks for hyphen (-), equal sign (=), brackets ([]), colon (:), curly single quote (‘), comma (,), full stop (.) and slash (/).<ref name="Corruption" />

Schroeder's numerals<ref name="Eric Schroeder old" /> were also used; a monitor in the Death Watch hideout aforementioned Death Watch hideout in "The Mandalorian" used a completely different design for the numerals 0 and 1,<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> with the alternative version of the digit 1 also appearing on the [[Clothing/Legends|prison uniform]] of an unidentified [[Prisoner/Legends|inmate]] at the [[Royal prison/Legends|royal prison]] in "The Academy." In addition, the number 7 on the inmate uniform looks like the standard number 1.<ref name="The Academy" /> Siddiq's keyboard in "Corruption" features every numeral from 0 to 9.<ref name="Corruption" />
 
The [[Star Wars Insider 117|''Star Wars Insider'' 117]] article "[[The Duchess and the Jedi]]" also uses Schroeder's font. The telltale sign are the letters 'C' and 'M,' which match<ref name="The Duchess and the Jedi">{{InsiderCite|117|The Duchess and the Jedi}}</ref> those developed by Schroeder exactly.<ref name="Eric Schroeder old" /> Schroeder himself has noted that the original characters were incorrect and had subsequently updated them for version 2 of his font.<ref name="Eric Schroeder new" />

===Other uses===
The Mandalorian inscriptions on page 25 and 26 of [[Star Wars Insider 86|''Star Wars Insider'' 86]], used as top page illustrations for the article "[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]," translate as "Jango Fett [[Sai cha/Legends|lost his head]]" and "akod oya akod oya akod oya" respectively.<ref name="The Mandalorians: People and Culture">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>
